misconceptions.description: Treating global, descriptive reflection (liked it, learned a lot) as analytic evidence about a design feature
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites praise or general impressions as data without a named feature, behavior, or consequence
misconceptions.feedback: Use excerpts that connect a specific design feature to a behavior and a consequence. Global praise cannot be coded against a decision.

misconceptions.description: Applying vague valence labels to reflections instead of defined, observable codes that another coder could apply
misconceptions.trigger: learner sorts reflections as positive or good with no operational code definition
misconceptions.feedback: Define codes by an observable claim in the text so two coders could agree, rather than by overall feeling.

misconceptions.description: Treating learners' felt helpfulness or perceived learning as proof of measured learning gains
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims a learning effect solely from reflections that say the lesson helped
misconceptions.feedback: Reflection is evidence of perception. Pair it with a performance measure before claiming a learning effect.
